title: Cabinet Approves Three Percent DA Hike to 63 Percent From July 2026
excerpt: The hike in Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief benefits 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners, costs Rs 10,016.10 crore a year, and brings arrears from July 1.
body:
• The Union Cabinet on October 28 approved a 3 percentage point hike in Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief, raising the rate from 60% to 63% of basic pay or pension.
  • The hike is effective retrospectively from July 1, 2026, so arrears for July to October will be due to eligible employees and pensioners.
  • About 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners will benefit, at a combined annual cost of Rs 10,016.10 crore.
  • Reader check: on Rs 50,000 basic pay, DA rises from Rs 30,000 to Rs 31,500 a month, an extra Rs 1,500 before arrears.

The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved an additional instalment of Dearness Allowance for central government employees and Dearness Relief for pensioners, raising both from 60% to 63% of basic pay or basic pension with effect from July 1, 2026. The decision, announced ahead of Diwali, is intended to compensate for price rises and follows the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission, according to New Kerala, reporting the government release via ANI.

Who benefits and what it costs

The government put the number of beneficiaries at about 48.54 lakh serving employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners, more than 1.17 crore people in total. The combined annual financial implication for the exchequer is Rs 10,016.10 crore. Because the revision applies retrospectively from July 1, employees and pensioners will be entitled to arrears for the months already elapsed at the old rate.

https://x.com/PBSHABD/status/2115454251350794554

Dearness Allowance is paid to serving employees to offset inflation; Dearness Relief performs the same function for pensioners. Both are calculated as a percentage of basic pay or basic pension, so the cash gain rises with the basic amount. The Live Ahmedabad gave the illustration used by officials: an employee on Rs 50,000 basic pay sees the DA component move from Rs 30,000 to Rs 31,500 a month.

Older pay commissions and the wider pay picture

The Cabinet also revised rates for those still governed by older pay structures. Under the 6th Central Pay Commission, DA and DR rise by seven percentage points, from 262% to 269% of basic pay. Under the 5th Central Pay Commission, they rise by 14 percentage points, from 483% to 497%. Both changes also take effect from July 1, 2026.

The previous 7th Commission revision had raised DA to 60% from January 1, 2026. Revisions normally come twice a year, in January and July. This hike arrives while the 8th Central Pay Commission process is under way. The government announced its formation on November 3, 2025, with former Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai as chairperson and 18 months to report, placing the expected deadline around May 2027. Any new pay structure would still require government acceptance after that report.

Employee unions have pressed for DA to be merged with basic pay while the next revision is awaited, a step last taken in 2004 when 50% of DA was merged as Dearness Pay under the 5th Commission framework. The Finance Ministry told Parliament in December 2025 that no such merger proposal was under consideration, and the rise to 63% does not by itself trigger a merger, as there is no automatic provision for one.

What happens next

Ministries and departments will now issue implementation orders, after which the revised allowance should appear in salary and pension credits along with arrears from July. Pensioners drawing family or basic pension through central government schemes should check the credit against the 63% rate once disbursing banks apply the order. For NRI families supporting retired parents in India, the practical point is the arrears lump sum and the higher monthly DR from the July effective date, not only the headline 3% figure.
